note: Oracle for forge's crates.io FFI boundary modules (§9, issue #16). Hand-derived (R-CHAR-3). A boundary fn is a bodyless `fn` + `#[boundary("crate::path")]`: the foreign body is UNPROVEN, the contract is L1-enforced (runtime checks on every crossing). It certifies Level L1 with a boundary flag + the foreign target — NOT L3. slag-adjacent (§9): it is enumerable in the TCB. NOTE: these programs require the #16 parser extension (bodyless-fn + the #[boundary] attribute) — they do NOT parse before #16; the builder confirms they parse + certify post-build.

certifies_l1_boundary.name: foreign_id
certifies_l1_boundary.program: #[boundary("ext::foreign_id")] fn foreign_id(x: u32) -> u32 req x < 100 ens result == x fx pure ;
certifies_l1_boundary.why: A foreign fn given a Thermite contract; the body is foreign (unproven) so it cannot reach L3 — it certifies L1 with the contract enforced at the crossing (req x<100 checked before, ens result==x checked after), boundary flag set, target recorded for the TCB enumeration.

reject.name: bodyless_without_boundary
reject.program: fn nope(x: u32) -> u32 req x < 100 ens result == x fx pure ;
reject.why: A bodyless `fn` WITHOUT #[boundary] must be a parse ERROR (OQ-2): the ;-body is only valid for a boundary fn; a normal fn missing its body must not silently become a boundary fn.

reject.name: boundary_vacuous_contract
reject.program: #[boundary("ext::g")] fn g(x: u32) -> u32 req true ens true fx pure ;
reject.why: boundary is slag-adjacent: it exempts PROVING, not STATING. A vacuous contract (ens true) on a boundary fn is still rejected by the §7.1 structural triage.
